CHAPTER III – MEMBERSHIP

3.1 Eligibility for Membership:
Any person who is competent to contract under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, and who
intends to reside in or use the premises of the Society for residential purposes, shall be
eligible for membership of the Society, subject to the provisions of the Act, the Rules, and
these Bylaws.

3.2 Application for Membership:
Every person desiring to become a member shall apply in the prescribed form, which shall be
accompanied by the entrance fee and the share capital amount as may be determined by the
General Body from time to time. The application shall be considered by the Managing
Committee at its next meeting, and the decision of the Managing Committee shall be
communicated to the applicant in writing.

3.3 Admission of Members:
The Managing Committee shall have the power to admit new members. The admission shall be
subject to the approval of the General Body at its next meeting. No person shall be admitted
as a member unless his or her application has been approved by the Managing Committee and
the admission fee and share capital have been paid in full.

3.4 Register of Members:
The Society shall maintain a Register of Members containing the full name, father’s or
husband’s name, occupation, address, date of admission, number of shares held, and such
other particulars as may be required by the Act or the Rules. The Register shall be open for
inspection by any member at the registered office during office hours.

3.5 Cessation of Membership:
Membership shall cease on death, transfer of all shares and interest in the Society, resignation
accepted by the Managing Committee, or expulsion in accordance with the provisions of the
Act and these Bylaws.

3.6 Transfer of Shares and Interest:
A member may transfer his or her shares and interest in the Society to any person eligible for
membership, subject to the approval of the Managing Committee. The transfer shall not be
effective until the transferee has been admitted as a member and the transfer has been duly
registered in the books of the Society.

3.7 Rights and Liabilities of Members:
Every member shall have the right to attend and vote at the General Body meetings, to inspect
the books and records of the Society as provided by law, and to receive a copy of the balance
sheet and audit report. Every member shall be liable to pay the entrance fee, share capital,
periodical charges, and such other sums as may be lawfully levied by the Society.

CHAPTER IV – SHARE CAPITAL

4.1 Authorised Share Capital:
The authorised share capital of the Society shall be Rs. 5,00,000 (Rupees Five Lakhs only)
divided into 5,000 shares of Rs. 100 (Rupees One Hundred) each.
4.4 Reduction of Share Capital:
The share capital of the Society shall not be reduced except with the prior approval of the
Registrar and in accordance with the provisions of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act,
1960, and the Rules framed thereunder.

4.5 Calls on Shares:
The Managing Committee may, from time to time, make calls upon the members in respect of
any moneys unpaid on their shares. Each call shall specify the amount and the date on which
it is payable. Not less than fourteen days’ notice in writing shall be given of any such call. A
member failing to pay any call on or before the appointed day shall be liable to pay interest at
the rate of ten percent per annum from the day appointed for payment to the time of actual
payment.

4.6 Forfeiture of Shares:
If a member fails to pay any call or instalment of a call on the day appointed for payment
thereof, the Managing Committee may, at any time thereafter during such time as the call
remains unpaid, serve a notice on such member demanding payment of the amount due,
together with interest. The notice shall name a further day (not earlier than fourteen days
from the date of service) on or before which the payment is required to be made. If the
requirements of such notice are not complied with, the shares in respect of which the call was
made may be forfeited by a resolution of the Managing Committee. A person whose shares
have been forfeited shall cease to be a member of the Society, but shall remain liable to pay
all moneys due and payable by him or her at the date of forfeiture.

5.1 Annual General Body Meeting:
The Annual General Body Meeting of the Society shall be held within six months after the
close of every financial year. The meeting shall be held on a Sunday or on a public holiday,
at the registered office of the Society or at any other place within the local limits of the city
of Pune, as the Managing Committee may decide. Notice of the meeting, together with the
agenda, shall be sent to every member at least fourteen days before the date of the meeting.

5.2 Special General Body Meeting:
The Chairman, or in his absence the Secretary, may call a Special General Body Meeting at
any time. The Managing Committee shall call such a meeting upon a requisition in writing
signed by not less than one-tenth of the total number of members. The requisition shall state
the business to be transacted. Upon receipt of a valid requisition, the Managing Committee
shall call the meeting within twenty-one days. If the Managing Committee fails to call the
meeting, the requisitionists may themselves call the meeting, and the expenses thereof shall
be borne by the Society.

5.3 Quorum:
Fifteen members personally present shall form the quorum for a General Body Meeting. If
within half an hour from the time appointed for the meeting a quorum is not present, the
meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the next week at the same time and place.
At the adjourned meeting, the members present shall form the quorum, and they may
transact the business for which the meeting was originally convened.

5.4 Chairman of the Meeting:
The Chairman of the Managing Committee shall preside over the General Body Meetings. In
his absence, the members present shall elect one of themselves to preside over the meeting.

5.5 Voting:
Every member shall have one vote. Voting may be by show of hands or by secret ballot, as
decided by the members present. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall have
a casting vote. No member shall vote by proxy.
6.3 Duties of the Chairman:
The Chairman shall preside over all meetings of the Managing Committee and the General Body. The Chairman shall supervise the working of the Managing Committee and shall have the power to authenticate the minutes of the meetings. The Chairman shall also have the power to incur expenditure on behalf of the Society up to a limit of ₹25,000 per instance for emergent repairs, subject to ratification by the Managing Committee at its next meeting.

6.4 Duties of the Vice-Chairman:
The Vice-Chairman shall perform the duties of the Chairman in the absence of the Chairman. The Vice-Chairman shall also assist the Chairman in the discharge of his duties and shall carry out such other functions as may be assigned to him by the Managing Committee from time to time.

6.5 Duties of the Secretary:
The Secretary shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Society and shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the affairs of the Society. The Secretary shall:
a) Issue notices for and prepare the agenda for all meetings of the Managing Committee and the General Body.
b) Record and maintain the minutes of all meetings of the Managing Committee and the General Body.
c) Maintain the register of members, the register of shares, and all other statutory registers required under the Act and the Rules.
d) Conduct the correspondence of the Society and preserve all letters, documents, and papers belonging to the Society.
e) Place before the Managing Committee all applications for membership, transfer of shares, and other matters requiring the attention of the Committee.
f) Be responsible for the safe custody of the common seal of the Society. The common seal shall not be affixed to any instrument except in the presence of the Chairman and the Treasurer, who shall sign the instrument as witnesses.
g) Submit to the Deputy Registrar all returns, reports, and statements as required under the Act and the Rules.
h) Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the Managing Committee from time to time.

**8. DISPUTE RESOLUTION**

**8.1 General**
All disputes arising out of the working of the Society, including disputes between the Society and any member, between members, and between the Society and any person claiming through a member, shall be referred to the Registrar of Co-operative Societies in accordance with Section 91 of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960, as may be amended from time to time. The jurisdiction for such reference shall be the office of the Deputy Registrar having territorial jurisdiction over the area in which the Society is situated.

**8.2 Internal Grievance Mechanism**
Before approaching the Registrar, a member shall first exhaust the internal grievance mechanism provided under these bylaws, unless the dispute is of an urgent nature or involves a sum exceeding ₹50,000, in which case the member may approach the Registrar directly. The internal mechanism shall operate as follows:

a) The member shall submit a written complaint to the Secretary of the Society, specifying the nature of the grievance, the relief sought, and the relevant clause of these bylaws or the Act under which the grievance arises. The complaint shall be dated and signed by the complainant, and shall be acknowledged by the Secretary on receipt, noting the date and time of receipt.

b) The Secretary shall place the complaint before the Managing Committee at its next meeting, which shall ordinarily be held within fifteen days of the receipt of the complaint. The Managing Committee shall consider the complaint and pass a reasoned resolution thereon within thirty days of receipt of the complaint. The Secretary shall communicate the decision in writing to the complainant by post or by email to the address registered with the Society.

c) If the complainant is not satisfied with the decision of the Managing Committee, or if the Managing Committee fails to decide the complaint within the period of thirty days specified above, the complainant may, within thirty days of the communication of the decision or the expiry of the said period, as the case may be, refer the matter to the Registrar. The Secretary shall, on request, provide the complainant with a copy of the minutes of the meeting at which the complaint was considered, along with the resolution passed thereon.

d) Nothing in this clause shall prevent the Managing Committee from attempting an amicable settlement of the dispute through mediation, conciliation, or arbitration, provided that such attempt shall not delay the disposal of the complaint beyond the period specified in sub-clause (b) above.

**8.3 Appointment of Arbitrator**
In the event that the Registrar refers any dispute to arbitration under Section 93 of the Act, the Society shall cooperate fully with the arbitrator so appointed. The Managing Committee shall nominate a representative to appear on behalf of the Society and shall provide all relevant records, minutes, and correspondence to the arbitrator as may be required. The costs of arbitration shall be borne as directed by the arbitrator, or in the absence of such direction, equally by the parties to the dispute.

**8.4 Effect of Pending Dispute**
The pendency of any dispute before the Registrar or arbitrator shall not operate as a stay on the implementation of any decision of the Managing Committee or the General Body, unless a specific stay order is obtained from the competent authority. However, the Managing Committee may, at its discretion, defer the implementation of any decision which is the subject matter of a dispute, if it is of the opinion that such deferment is necessary in the interest of the Society or to avoid multiplicity of proceedings.

The financial year of the Society shall commence on the 1st day of April of every year and shall end on the 31st day of March of the following year.

b) The Society shall also maintain a Reserve Fund for meeting unforeseen expenses and contingencies. The contribution to the Reserve Fund shall be decided by the General Body on the recommendation of the Managing Committee.

c) The amounts standing to the credit of the Sinking Fund and the Reserve Fund shall be invested in a scheduled bank or in such other securities as may be approved by the General Body. The investment shall be made in the name of the Society.

**10.4 Other Funds**

The Society may, with the approval of the General Body, create such other funds as may be necessary for the efficient functioning of the Society, including but not limited to a Building Repair Fund, a Welfare Fund, and a Festival Fund.

**10.5 Budget**

a) The Managing Committee shall prepare an annual budget of income and expenditure for the ensuing financial year and place it before the General Body for approval at the Annual General Meeting.

b) The budget shall show, inter alia, the estimated income from maintenance charges, interest on investments, and other sources, and the estimated expenditure on salaries, repairs, maintenance, insurance, electricity, water charges, audit fees, and other items.

c) No expenditure shall be incurred in excess of the budgeted amount without the prior approval of the General Body, except in cases of emergency where the Managing Committee may incur expenditure up to ₹25,000, subject to ratification by the General Body at its next meeting.

**10.6 Accounts and Books of Account**

c) The Managing Committee shall maintain a register of all repairs carried out, showing the date, nature of repair, name of the contractor, and the amount paid. This register shall be open to inspection by any member at all reasonable times.

d) No member shall carry out any structural changes to their own flat which may, in the opinion of the Managing Committee, endanger the safety of the building or affect the common services. Any such work shall be undertaken only after obtaining prior written permission from the Managing Committee.

**10.9 Safety and Security**

a) The Society shall maintain adequate fire-fighting equipment, including fire extinguishers on every floor, and shall have them serviced at least once a year by a licensed agency.

b) The Managing Committee shall ensure that the staircase and corridors are free of obstruction at all times and that no inflammable material is stored in the common areas.

c) The Society shall engage security personnel for the gate and common areas, and may install CCTV cameras at strategic locations. The footage shall be preserved for a minimum of 30 days.

d) The Managing Committee shall make arrangements for the annual testing of the electrical installations and the lift, and a record of such tests shall be kept in the Society's office.

c) Elections shall be held every five years, or earlier if the Managing Committee is dissolved by the General Body or by the Deputy Registrar, Co-operative Societies, Pune.

**11.2 Election Procedure**

a) The Managing Committee shall appoint an Election Officer at least sixty (60) days before the date fixed for elections. The Election Officer shall not be a member of the Managing Committee or a candidate for election.

b) Notice of election, along with the list of eligible voters, shall be displayed on the Society notice board and circulated by email at least thirty (30) days before the date of election.

c) Any member desirous of contesting the election shall file their nomination with the Election Officer in the prescribed form, accompanied by a deposit of ₹500, which shall be refunded if the candidate secures at least five (5) votes or is elected.

d) Voting shall be by secret ballot. The Election Officer shall arrange for a ballot box and ensure the secrecy of the ballot.

e) In the event of a tie, the matter shall be decided by draw of lots in the presence of the Election Officer and the candidates concerned.

f) The result of the election shall be declared on the same day and shall be displayed on the notice board. The newly elected Managing Committee shall assume office at the first meeting held after the election.

**11.3 Casual Vacancies**

a) If a seat on the Managing Committee falls vacant due to death, resignation, disqualification, or otherwise, the remaining members of the Managing Committee shall co-opt a member to fill the vacancy. The co-opted member shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the vacating member.

b) If the number of remaining members falls below the quorum required for a meeting (five members), the Managing Committee shall within thirty (30) days call a special General Body meeting to elect a new Managing Committee for the remaining term.

**11.4 Disqualification of Members**

a) have been convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude;
b) are in arrears of Society dues for more than six (6) months;
c) have been declared insolvent;
d) have been removed from the Managing Committee by the General Body for misconduct or breach of trust.

a) The Annual General Meeting of the Society shall be held within six (6) months of the close of the financial year, i.e., on or before 30th September of each year.

b) The agenda for the AGM shall include:

i. Reading and confirmation of the minutes of the previous General Body meeting;

   iii. Presentation of the annual budget for the current financial year;

a) A Special General Body Meeting may be called by the Managing Committee at any time, and shall be called by the Secretary within fifteen (15) days of receipt of a requisition signed by not less than one-tenth (1/10th) of the total number of members entitled to vote.

b) The requisition shall state the purpose for which the meeting is required. No business other than that stated in the requisition shall be transacted at such meeting.

c) The Managing Committee shall fix the date, time, and venue of the Special General Body Meeting, which shall be held within thirty (30) days of the date of receipt of the requisition.

**12.3 Notice of General Body Meetings**

a) Written notice of every General Body Meeting, along with the agenda, shall be served upon every member at least fourteen (14) days before the date of the meeting. The notice may be served by:
   i. personal delivery and acknowledgement;
   ii. posting by ordinary mail to the member's registered address; or
   iii. electronic mail to the member's registered email address, provided the member has opted for electronic communication.

b) The notice and agenda shall also be displayed on the Society's notice board and, if available, on the Society's website.

c) No business other than that stated in the agenda shall be transacted at a General Body Meeting without the consent of the Chair and the majority of members present.

**12.4 Quorum**

a) The quorum for a General Body Meeting shall be one-fifth (1/5th) of the total number of members entitled to vote.

b) If within thirty (30) minutes of the appointed time a quorum is not present, the meeting shall stand adjourned for half an hour. At the adjourned meeting, the members present shall form the quorum, provided that the adjourned meeting is held not less than seven (7) days after the original meeting and notice of the adjourned meeting is given to all members.

**12.5 Chairperson of the Meeting**

The Chairperson of the Managing Committee, or in their absence, the Vice-Chairperson, shall preside over the General Body Meeting. In the absence of both, the members present shall elect one of themselves to chair the meeting.

a) Each member present in person shall have one vote. Voting by proxy shall not be permitted.

c) For resolutions relating to the matters specified in Bylaw No. 13, voting shall be by secret ballot.

**12.7 Minutes of the Meeting**

The minutes of every General Body Meeting shall be recorded by the Secretary and shall be confirmed at the next General Body Meeting. The minutes, once confirmed, shall be signed by the Chairperson of that meeting and shall be preserved in the Minutes Book.

The following matters shall be decided by a special resolution, i.e., a resolution passed by a majority of not less than three-fourths (3/4th) of the members present and voting at a General Body Meeting of which not less than twenty-one (21) days' notice has been given:

Every person desiring to become a member shall apply in the prescribed form, which shall be
accompanied by the entrance fee and the share capital amount as may be determined by the
General Body from time to time. The application shall be considered by the Managing
Committee at its next meeting, and the decision of the Managing Committee shall be
communicated to the applicant in writing.

3.3 Admission of Members:
The Managing Committee shall have the power to admit new members. The admission shall be
subject to the approval of the General Body at its next meeting. No person shall be admitted
as a member unless his or her application has been approved by the Managing Committee and
the admission fee and share capital have been paid in full.

3.4 Register of Members:
The Society shall maintain a Register of Members containing the full name, father’s or
husband’s name, occupation, address, date of admission, number of shares held, and such
other particulars as may be required by the Act or the Rules. The Register shall be open for
inspection by any member at the registered office during office hours.

3.5 Cessation of Membership:
Membership shall cease on death, transfer of all shares and interest in the Society, resignation
accepted by the Managing Committee, or expulsion in accordance with the provisions of the
Act and these Bylaws.

3.6 Transfer of Shares and Interest:
A member may transfer his or her shares and interest in the Society to any person eligible for
membership, subject to the approval of the Managing Committee. The transfer shall not be
effective until the transferee has been admitted as a member and the transfer has been duly
registered in the books of the Society.

3.7 Rights and Liabilities of Members:
Every member shall have the right to attend and vote at the General Body meetings, to inspect
the books and records of the Society as provided by law, and to receive a copy of the balance
sheet and audit report. Every member shall be liable to pay the entrance fee, share capital,
periodical charges, and such other sums as may be lawfully levied by the Society.

The share capital of the Society shall not be reduced except with the prior approval of the
Registrar and in accordance with the provisions of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act,

The Managing Committee may, from time to time, make calls upon the members in respect of
any moneys unpaid on their shares. Each call shall specify the amount and the date on which

member failing to pay any call on or before the appointed day shall be liable to pay interest at
the rate of ten percent per annum from the day appointed for payment to the time of actual
payment.

4.6 Forfeiture of Shares:
If a member fails to pay any call or instalment of a call on the day appointed for payment
thereof, the Managing Committee may, at any time thereafter during such time as the call
remains unpaid, serve a notice on such member demanding payment of the amount due,
together with interest. The notice shall name a further day (not earlier than fourteen days
from the date of service) on or before which the payment is required to be made. If the
requirements of such notice are not complied with, the shares in respect of which the call was
made may be forfeited by a resolution of the Managing Committee. A person whose shares
have been forfeited shall cease to be a member of the Society, but shall remain liable to pay
all moneys due and payable by him or her at the date of forfeiture.

within half an hour from the time appointed for the meeting a quorum is not present, the

decided by the members present. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall have

**7.4 Powers of the Maintenance Committee**

a) To engage the services of plumbers, electricians, carpenters, and other skilled workers for the execution of minor repairs and maintenance work, subject to the budgetary limits fixed by the Managing Committee.
b) To purchase such materials, tools, and consumables as may be necessary for the maintenance of the Society, provided that the total expenditure on any single purchase shall not exceed Rs. 10,000 without the prior approval of the Managing Committee.
c) To recommend to the Managing Committee the appointment of contractors for major repair works or for annual maintenance contracts.
d) To inspect any part of the Society premises at any reasonable time to ascertain the need for repairs or maintenance.
e) To call upon any member or occupant to desist from causing damage to the common areas or from creating a nuisance, and to report such instances to the Managing Committee for further action.

**7.5 Meetings of the Maintenance Committee**

The Maintenance Committee shall meet at least once in every two months, and more often as may be necessary. The Head of the Maintenance Committee shall preside over the meetings. In the absence of the Head, the members present shall elect one of themselves to preside. The quorum for a meeting of the Maintenance Committee shall be one-third of its total members or two, whichever is higher. The proceedings of every meeting of the Maintenance Committee shall be recorded in a minute book maintained for the purpose, and a copy of the minutes shall be circulated to all members of the Managing Committee within seven days of the meeting.

The Maintenance Committee shall submit a report of its activities and the expenditure incurred by it to the Managing Committee at every meeting of the Managing Committee. The report shall be in writing and shall contain details of the works executed, the amounts spent, and the receipts and vouchers in support thereof. The Maintenance Committee shall also place before the Managing Committee an estimate of the likely expenditure on maintenance for the ensuing quarter, for the purpose of budgetary planning.

Any expenditure incurred under this clause shall be reported to the Managing Committee at its next meeting, along with the details of the emergency and the action taken.

**7.9 Maintenance Committee Meeting Frequency**

The Maintenance Committee shall meet at least once in every month, and more often as may be necessary.

The schedule of meetings shall be prepared by the Head of the Maintenance Committee at the beginning of each financial year, and a copy of the schedule shall be circulated to all members of the Managing Committee. The schedule shall be revised as and when necessary.

The quorum for a meeting of the Maintenance Committee shall be one-third of its total members or two, whichever is higher.

The proceedings of every meeting of the Maintenance Committee shall be recorded in a minute book maintained for the purpose, and a copy of the minutes shall be circulated to all members of the Managing Committee within seven days of the meeting.

The Maintenance Committee shall maintain a register of all complaints received from members regarding maintenance issues, and shall record the action taken thereon. The register shall be open for inspection by any member of the Society at the Society office during working hours.

**7.10 Decision-Making and Voting**

All decisions of the Maintenance Committee shall be taken by a majority of the members present and voting. In the case of an equality of votes, the Head of the Maintenance Committee, or the person presiding over the meeting, shall have a casting vote.

No decision of the Maintenance Committee shall be valid unless it is taken at a meeting duly convened and held in accordance with the provisions of these bylaws.

**8. DISPUTE RESOLUTION**

**8.1 General**
All disputes arising out of the working of the Society, including disputes between the Society and any member, between members, and between the Society and any person claiming through a member, shall be referred to the Registrar of Co-operative Societies in accordance with Section 91 of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960, as may be amended from time to time. The jurisdiction for such reference shall be the office of the Deputy Registrar having territorial jurisdiction over the area in which the Society is situated.

**8.2 Internal Grievance Mechanism**
Before approaching the Registrar, a member shall first exhaust the internal grievance mechanism provided under these bylaws, unless the dispute is of an urgent nature or involves a sum exceeding ₹50,000, in which case the member may approach the Registrar directly. The internal mechanism shall operate as follows:

a) The member shall submit a written complaint to the Secretary of the Society, specifying the nature of the grievance, the relief sought, and the relevant clause of these bylaws or the Act under which the grievance arises. The complaint shall be dated and signed by the complainant, and shall be acknowledged by the Secretary on receipt, noting the date and time of receipt.

b) The Secretary shall place the complaint before the Managing Committee at its next meeting, which shall ordinarily be held within fifteen days of the receipt of the complaint. The Managing Committee shall consider the complaint and pass a reasoned resolution thereon within thirty days of receipt of the complaint. The Secretary shall communicate the decision in writing to the complainant by post or by email to the address registered with the Society.

c) If the complainant is not satisfied with the decision of the Managing Committee, or if the Managing Committee fails to decide the complaint within the period of thirty days specified above, the complainant may, within thirty days of the communication of the decision or the expiry of the said period, as the case may be, refer the matter to the Registrar. The Secretary shall, on request, provide the complainant with a copy of the minutes of the meeting at which the complaint was considered, along with the resolution passed thereon.

d) Nothing in this clause shall prevent the Managing Committee from attempting an amicable settlement of the dispute through mediation, conciliation, or arbitration, provided that such attempt shall not delay the disposal of the complaint beyond the period specified in sub-clause (b) above.

**8.3 Appointment of Arbitrator**
In the event that the Registrar refers any dispute to arbitration under Section 93 of the Act, the Society shall cooperate fully with the arbitrator so appointed. The Managing Committee shall nominate a representative to appear on behalf of the Society and shall provide all relevant records, minutes, and correspondence to the arbitrator as may be required. The costs of arbitration shall be borne as directed by the arbitrator, or in the absence of such direction, equally by the parties to the dispute.

**8.4 Effect of Pending Dispute**
The pendency of any dispute before the Registrar or arbitrator shall not operate as a stay on the implementation of any decision of the Managing Committee or the General Body, unless a specific stay order is obtained from the competent authority. However, the Managing Committee may, at its discretion, defer the implementation of any decision which is the subject matter of a dispute, if it is of the opinion that such deferment is necessary in the interest of the Society or to avoid multiplicity of proceedings.

**CHAPTER 10: FINANCE, BUDGETING, AND AUDIT**

**10.1 Financial Year**

The financial year of the Society shall commence on the 1st day of April of every year and shall end on the 31st day of March of the following year.

**10.2 Maintenance Charges**

a) Every member shall pay monthly maintenance charges to the Society, as determined by the Managing Committee from time to time and ratified by the General Body at the Annual General Meeting. The charges shall be calculated on the basis of the carpet area of the flat, the number of occupants, and the amenities availed.

b) The monthly maintenance charges shall be payable on or before the 10th day of each calendar month. A late fee of ₹100 per month or part thereof shall be levied for payment received after the due date. The Managing Committee may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, waive the late fee in deserving cases.

c) The Managing Committee shall, at the beginning of each financial year, circulate a statement showing the proposed monthly maintenance charges for the ensuing year, along with the basis of calculation, to all members at least fifteen days before the Annual General Meeting.

**10.3 Sinking Fund and Reserve Fund**

a) The Society shall maintain a Sinking Fund for the purpose of major repairs, replacements, and reconstruction of the building and common amenities. Every member shall contribute to the Sinking Fund at the rate of not less than 0.25% per annum of the construction cost of the building, as determined by the Managing Committee and approved by the General Body.

b) The Society shall also maintain a Reserve Fund for meeting unforeseen expenses and contingencies. The contribution to the Reserve Fund shall be decided by the General Body on the recommendation of the Managing Committee.

c) The amounts standing to the credit of the Sinking Fund and the Reserve Fund shall be invested in a scheduled bank or in such other securities as may be approved by the General Body. The investment shall be made in the name of the Society.

**10.4 Other Funds**

The Society may, with the approval of the General Body, create such other funds as may be necessary for the efficient functioning of the Society, including but not limited to a Building Repair Fund, a Welfare Fund, and a Festival Fund.

**10.5 Budget**

a) The Managing Committee shall prepare an annual budget of income and expenditure for the ensuing financial year and place it before the General Body for approval at the Annual General Meeting.

b) The budget shall show, inter alia, the estimated income from maintenance charges, interest on investments, and other sources, and the estimated expenditure on salaries, repairs, maintenance, insurance, electricity, water charges, audit fees, and other items.

c) No expenditure shall be incurred in excess of the budgeted amount without the prior approval of the General Body, except in cases of emergency where the Managing Committee may incur expenditure up to ₹25,000, subject to ratification by the General Body at its next meeting.

**10.6 Accounts and Books of Account**

a) The Managing Committee shall cause to be kept proper books of account with respect to all sums of money received and expended by the Society and the matters in respect of which the receipt and expenditure take place.

c) Elections shall be held every five years, or earlier if the Managing Committee is dissolved by the General Body or by the Deputy Registrar, Co-operative Societies, Pune.

**11.2 Election Procedure**

a) The Managing Committee shall appoint an Election Officer at least sixty (60) days before the date fixed for elections. The Election Officer shall not be a member of the Managing Committee or a candidate for election.

b) Notice of election, along with the list of eligible voters, shall be displayed on the Society notice board and circulated by email at least thirty (30) days before the date of election.

c) Any member desirous of contesting the election shall file their nomination with the Election Officer in the prescribed form, accompanied by a deposit of ₹500, which shall be refunded if the candidate secures at least five (5) votes or is elected.

d) Voting shall be by secret ballot. The Election Officer shall arrange for a ballot box and ensure the secrecy of the ballot.

e) In the event of a tie, the matter shall be decided by draw of lots in the presence of the Election Officer and the candidates concerned.

f) The result of the election shall be declared on the same day and shall be displayed on the notice board. The newly elected Managing Committee shall assume office at the first meeting held after the election.

**11.3 Casual Vacancies**

a) If a seat on the Managing Committee falls vacant due to death, resignation, disqualification, or otherwise, the remaining members of the Managing Committee shall co-opt a member to fill the vacancy. The co-opted member shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the vacating member.

**12.2 Special General Body Meeting (SGM)**

a) A Special General Body Meeting may be called by the Managing Committee at any time, and shall be called by the Secretary within fifteen (15) days of receipt of a requisition signed by not less than one-tenth (1/10th) of the total number of members entitled to vote.

b) The requisition shall state the purpose for which the meeting is required. No business other than that stated in the requisition shall be transacted at such meeting.

c) The Managing Committee shall fix the date, time, and venue of the Special General Body Meeting, which shall be held within thirty (30) days of the date of receipt of the requisition.

**12.3 Notice of General Body Meetings**

a) Written notice of every General Body Meeting, along with the agenda, shall be served upon every member at least fourteen (14) days before the date of the meeting. The notice may be served by:
   i. personal delivery and acknowledgement;
   ii. posting by ordinary mail to the member's registered address; or
   iii. electronic mail to the member's registered email address, provided the member has opted for electronic communication.

b) The notice and agenda shall also be displayed on the Society's notice board and, if available, on the Society's website.

c) No business other than that stated in the agenda shall be transacted at a General Body Meeting without the consent of the Chair and the majority of members present.

**12.4 Quorum**

a) The quorum for a General Body Meeting shall be one-fifth (1/5th) of the total number of members entitled to vote.

b) If within thirty (30) minutes of the appointed time a quorum is not present, the meeting shall stand adjourned for half an hour. At the adjourned meeting, the members present shall form the quorum, provided that the adjourned meeting is held not less than seven (7) days after the original meeting and notice of the adjourned meeting is given to all members.

**12.5 Chairperson of the Meeting**

The Chairperson of the Managing Committee, or in their absence, the Vice-Chairperson, shall preside over the General Body Meeting. In the absence of both, the members present shall elect one of themselves to chair the meeting.

**12.6 Voting**

a) Each member present in person shall have one vote. Voting by proxy shall not be permitted.

b) Save as otherwise provided in these Bylaws, decisions at a General Body Meeting shall be taken by a simple majority of the members present and voting. In case of an equality of votes, the Chairperson shall have a casting vote.

c) For resolutions relating to the matters specified in Bylaw No. 13, voting shall be by secret ballot.

**12.7 Minutes of the Meeting**

The minutes of every General Body Meeting shall be recorded by the Secretary and shall be confirmed at the next General Body Meeting. The minutes, once confirmed, shall be signed by the Chairperson of that meeting and shall be preserved in the Minutes Book.

---

**BYLAW NO. 13 – RESERVED MATTERS AND SPECIAL RESOLUTIONS**

**13.1 Matters Requiring Special Resolution**

The following matters shall be decided by a special resolution, i.e., a resolution passed by a majority of not less than three-fourths (3/4th) of the members present and voting at a General Body Meeting of which not less than twenty-one (21) days' notice has been given:

a) Amendment of the Bylaws;
b) Sale, mortgage, lease, or other transfer of the Society's immovable property;
c) Raising of a loan or loans exceeding fifty percent (50%) of the value of the Society's immovable property;
d) Change of the name or address of the Society;
e) Amalgamation or division of the Society;
f) Dissolution of the Society.
